findings.title: Deleting cache does not invalidate the connected-calendars query
findings.body: The deleteCache mutation only shows a toast and invokes the optional onSuccess callback, unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component which invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars on settle. Callers are not required to pass onSuccess (the wrapper forwards an optional prop), so after a successful deletion the connectedCalendars query keeps returning the old cacheUpdatedAt, hasCache stays true, and the UI continues to show the stale timestamp and a Delete action for cache that no longer exists until some unrelated refetch occurs.

findings.title: Cache status counts expired cache entries as live cache
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups rows by credentialId and returns _max(updatedAt) with no expiresAt filter. CalendarCache rows are not removed when they expire (getCachedAvailability treats expiresAt < now as a miss, but the row remains), so the new UI will display 'Cache Status / Last updated' and offer Delete for credentials whose only cache rows are already expired and are never actually served.

findings.title: Authorization failure is thrown as a generic Error instead of a TRPCError
findings.body: When the credential does not belong to the session user the handler throws a plain Error('Credential not found or access denied'). tRPC wraps non-TRPCError throws as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, so a client error (unknown or foreign credentialId) is reported and logged as a server failure and callers cannot distinguish it. This should be a TRPCError (e.g. NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN) with an appropriate code.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is always formatted in en-US regardless of user locale
findings.body: The component localizes all strings through useLocale but formats cacheUpdatedAt with Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...). Users on non-US locales will see US-style dates/times (e.g. month/day order) in an otherwise localized UI; the formatter should use the user's locale returned by useLocale/i18n.

findings.title: Unconditional empty updateMany marks every SelectedCalendar for the credential as freshly updated
findings.body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) after the per-event-type loop. The write is unconditional and credential-wide: it bumps updatedAt on every SelectedCalendar row for the credential, including event-type-scoped rows and rows whose calendars were not in the fetched groups, and it runs even when the grouped map is empty and no cache entry was written. Anything reading SelectedCalendar.updatedAt as a freshness marker will be told calendars were refreshed when no cache fetch happened, and every cache population now pays an extra blanket UPDATE.

findings.title: Webhook helper uses macOS-only sed syntax and still reports success on Linux
findings.body: The in-place edit uses BSD/macOS syntax 'sed -i '' -E ...'. With GNU sed the empty string is taken as the script, the substitution is treated as a filename, and the edit fails; because the script has no 'set -e' or error check it then prints 'Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL ...' anyway, leaving developers on Linux with a stale or missing webhook URL while believing it was set. The script is also unrelated to the calendar-cache feature it ships with.

findings.title: dev:cron now shells out to unpinned npx tsx, which is not a declared dependency
findings.body: The script was changed from ts-node (declared in devDependencies) to 'npx tsx cron-tester.ts', but tsx is not declared in apps/web's dependencies. npx will resolve and download whatever latest tsx is available at run time (failing offline and bypassing the lockfile's pinned versions), making the dev script non-reproducible. This unrelated tooling change should either declare tsx as a devDependency or be dropped.

findings.title: No tests cover the new destructive deleteCache endpoint or cache-status query
findings.body: The PR adds a destructive, ownership-checked tRPC mutation, a new groupBy repository method, and cache-status enrichment of connectedCalendars, but adds or updates no tests. The security-critical cases are unverified: deleting cache for one's own credential succeeds, deleting another user's credentialId is rejected and deletes nothing, and getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns the latest updatedAt per credential. A regression in the findFirst ownership check would let any authenticated user wipe another user's calendar cache without any test failing.
